identity.narrative: Clean-room Dungeon Master-family engine using authenticated original media. Current primary documentation records bounded startup/runtime coverage for DM1 on DOS, Atari ST, Amiga and FM Towns; CSB on Amiga, Atari ST and FM Towns; and DM2 on DOS, Amiga, FM Towns and Macintosh. The latest receipts correct DM1 Amiga HD and DM2 FM Towns boot assertions and expand the cross-game startup matrix and diagnostics. These source-owned handoffs do not establish full campaign, save, display or audio parity; Nexus and Theron's Quest remain explicitly bounded, with authentic level/campaign consumers still incomplete. Evidence: https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/blob/main/docs/PROJECT_STATUS.md https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/7791b08de76e https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/17a20bdb465e The newest authenticated-media pass discovers the DM1 Amiga 3.6 archive from configured data roots, covers its root-menu scan, records an Amiga startup-media matrix and wires DM1 PC34 soundtrack selection to WAV playback. These remain bounded startup/audio receipts rather than full-game parity. Evidence: https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/d3b50c77c364455674d783c6bf4d4755777dbc44 https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/ec51d5c1b2f58b51b235fc2145abb384d55b597c https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/da1e85756e618dd321ec42257cb31afbb2b341d1 v3.0.376 receipts now cover DM1 Amiga 2.0 resume, the published Linux x86-64 AppImage under QEMU on an ARM64 VM, and the DM2 FM Towns selected-hero HUD icon sourced from authenticated interface data. They do not establish native x86-64 hardware, physical input, aura/panel completion or full visual parity. The release also publishes Android and iOS arm64 artifacts; publication alone is not runtime verification. Evidence: https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/releases/tag/v3.0.376 https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/e0cf778c39b039918d6b1ae1ebf18e23ec423b1a https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/f0c58017d243551f9dbf30ae5b28fb25172bd10e https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/1be613b14f3cef9e2323a3e2b6ed840e13f6c480 Current-main receipts add native Mac mini M4 DM1 title/door pacing into runtime and authenticated FM Towns startup checks for DM1, CSB and DM2. A four-run French Atari ST test also narrowed an earlier no-output incident to a plausible uninitialized-menu fallback, while explicitly leaving historical causation, physical input, display/palette and audible-speaker parity open. Evidence: https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/7256c2f693a8f2a609ebccfcb687f5e1f8c00868 https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/47bc75ce1f897306e74d2e79a0c053209684edd9 https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/3b729320e80658a8eae965f11c1b5f1bd880f5a3 Current-main Amiga work now paces DM1 A20 palette fades and title zooms against absolute 20 ms source deadlines rather than adding host VSync latency. An authentic Amiga v2.0 native Cocoa run on a Mac mini M4 completed the five-fade title in 1,698 ms (366 ms zoom, 500 ms hold, 166 ms final fade); this does not establish HiDPI/pixel parity or beam-line 152 timing. The authenticated Japanese FM Towns CSB save regression now asserts restored map 0, party position 13,13, direction 1 and four champions through direct launch and the live menu-resume route. Evidence: https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/1538eeab7f46d6318be1c6cd89a55a9edc6d5d87 https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/1d3f8e34d62d0cd9b95d74d9fd33b1bb35eb1a6e https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/087aed4bf4b977cb30805152519c82860ff2ed20 Current-main receipts add an authenticated DM2 Amiga viewport gate, bounded DOS viewport/HUD checks and a locked three-draw fresh-weather RNG bootstrap. Separate native Mac M4 tests keep live Retina input unresolved despite controlled 2x/mixed-geometry tests, and real-media startup reruns use dummy video/audio, so they do not establish physical display, input or speaker parity. A separate authenticated PC 3.4 path decodes the LZEXE-packed DOS selector preview. Targeted source-lock/native-build checks pass upstream, but the author explicitly retains original-frame comparison and full cross-platform visual parity as open. Evidence: https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/9a2b86019bfcd6bd513213bc21cd402a4f5adaf0 https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/2a85ec7e1801b58d22232fa11ccc5f18a0e9bd0d https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/41b103f29b4d7439d7445fb4e3578f9985e5cfab https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/3085c2f6d56e8088279b5207bfd46744a1dbbd24 The Apple IIGS path now decodes original dungeon worlds, graphics, startup/font, creature/effect metadata and sound, launches authenticated worlds through the CLI/M12 path, and connects native IIGS mirror recruitment. Primary recovered documentation explicitly identifies hidden Apple IIGS graphics.dat code as 65C816 code, supporting the added source architecture. Current changelog receipts also cover stereo DOC effects, Hall progression, inventory transfer, food use and carrying capacity; wall damage, sensors and full sound/presentation parity remain open. No Apple IIGS minimum RAM or host profile is inferred. Debug traces separately measure queue, source-outcome and present-return timing while explicitly marking physical scanout unmeasured. Evidence: https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/449d2322fcf641e88cf876a032ee2cc58ca96373 https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/e5b732073270bbb500d10919239185d212ad6d44 The authenticated DM1 Apple IIGS G20E/G21E editions now reach the first world through both direct CLI and M12 menu launch; the CLI route also accepts a native keyboard turn, and the original media archive is hash-checked before and after the run. The upstream check uses SDL dummy output, so original title/entrance presentation, audible DOC playback and complete-campaign parity remain open. A v3.0.387 preparation change is not represented as a published release because no corresponding release was available when checked. Evidence: https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/c9d9b0e0097242ea1a6f1e5fa29183c3e09bfabb Firestaff v3.0.391 is a published release. Its primary notes record DM1 PC34 selected-save restoration, authenticated English/Japanese CSB FM Towns loose-file startup, and Amiga 3.6 French/German graphic selection. Only seven of ten localized bitmap records are decoded for comparison, and upstream explicitly says these checks do not establish complete visual or gameplay parity. Evidence: https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/releases/tag/v3.0.391 https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/ebb10387f277af76683e3aadd27f97dab963d599 https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/d15a674ba936133e9b74b43af982051927f51207 Firestaff v3.0.397 reuses verified hashes for nested archive members while retaining archive freshness checks. On the tested Mac mini M4, the authentic five-game scan took 27.90 seconds cold and 12.35 seconds warm; other platforms and cold-cache performance remain explicitly unverified, and SDL dummy checks do not establish native display, physical input, audible output or complete parity.
